A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Uni-MMMU and provide readable text, figures, tables, and appendices. The benchmark and existing experiments match; v3 retains Appendices A–B and adds Appendix C. No material reading gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations on Uni-MMMU (Table 2), judge-validation results (Table 3), and experiments comparing generated and ground-truth intermediates (Table 4).

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports human–judge correlations in Section 4.3 and model-specific failure frequencies in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, model prompting and inference, deterministic parsers, and Qwen judge procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. The open-weights wording clarifies the existing judges without replacing them.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 885-instance benchmark covering Maze, Sliding Puzzle, Geometry, Jigsaw, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and Code Rendering. The added analyses concern retained tasks and introduce no new domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated unified, generation-only, and understanding-only model sets in Table 2 and the comparison configurations in Table 4 are unchanged. Human annotators and Gemini-2.5-pro remain the judge-validation comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 retains the 150-output binary Kappa validation and adds a 707-sample Code Rendering comparison using Pearson correlation on the full six-level scale. Appendix C adds failure-counting criteria. These extend the analysis protocol without revising the existing benchmark evaluation settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix C supplements Figure 3's qualitative cases with failure frequencies for Jigsaw, Code Rendering, and Maze. Section 4.3 additionally examines human–judge correspondence before binarizing Code Rendering scores. The existing oracle ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v3 adds Pearson correlation estimation to the existing Cohen's Kappa reporting. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new sample count does not establish an increase in experimental runs.

E6.justification: All existing scores in Tables 2–4 are unchanged. New results include Pearson correlations of 0.84 for Shape&Color and 0.76 for Position, plus Appendix C failure rates: for example, invalid Maze outputs occur for 15% of nano-banana, 84% of GPT, and 100% of Bagel outputs. Jigsaw and Code Rendering failure frequencies are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The task constraints, existing mathematical reasoning, and worked geometry example in Appendix A are unchanged. No formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same benchmark, dual-level evaluation, and generation–understanding synergy claims. Generation being the primary bottleneck was already claimed in v2. The added conclusion sentence concerns resource availability.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly attributes the majority of Sliding Puzzle and Geometry score degradation specifically to background/style drift and instruction-following lapses. The broader generation-bottleneck interpretation in Section 4.4 and the limitations in Section 7 are unchanged.

D1.justification: v3's conclusion explicitly states that code, datasets, evaluation tools, and judge configurations are released and provides a repository address; v2 provides a project-page link. Appendix A implementation details and Appendix B's A800 hardware, approximately 48 GPU-days, and default sampling settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion in Section 2, and comparison with prior benchmarks in Table 1 are unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits add a project-leader credit, clarify open-weights terminology and judge-selection rationale, expand Sections 4.3 and 5, and append Section C. The existing narrative and section order are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from the left to the right column on page 8, with accompanying text and reference reflow. Existing figures, table structures, and captions retain their content and design; the additional statistics appear in prose.

improvement.justification: The full-scale human–judge correlations add useful validation beyond v2's binary agreement analysis, while failure frequencies and explicit resource-access information improve documentation. The gains are limited by an internal inconsistency: Appendix C labels DreamSim distance below 0.2 as indicating irrelevant images, whereas retained Appendix A.1.4 says lower distance indicates better reconstruction. This weakens that Jigsaw statistic, but the independent validation addition still supports a modest overall improvement.
